title: Valid Parentheses
description: Check that every bracket in a string is closed by the right kind of bracket, in the right order.
statement:
The string `s` contains only the characters `(`, `)`, `[`, `]`, `{` and `}`. Return `True` if its brackets are balanced, and `False` otherwise.

Brackets are balanced when every opening bracket is closed by a bracket **of the same kind**, and they are closed in the right order: the most recently opened bracket that is still open must be the next one to close.

- The empty string is balanced.
- A closing bracket with nothing open to match it makes the string unbalanced, and so does an opening bracket that is never closed.

**Examples**

```python
is_valid("()[]{}")   # True
is_valid("([{}])")   # True
is_valid("(]")       # False: the wrong kind
is_valid("([)]")     # False: closed in the wrong order
```

Aim for O(n): the last tests have 200,000 characters.
tests: assert is_valid("(" * 100_000 + ")" * 100_000) == True, "too slow or wrong on 200,000 characters; deleting matched pairs over and over is O(n^2)"
assert is_valid("([{" * 30_000 + "}])" * 30_000) == True, "too slow or wrong on 180,000 characters nested ten thousand deep"
assert is_valid("(" * 100_000 + ")" * 99_999 + "]") == False, "wrong when only the very last bracket is the wrong kind"
hints: The most recently opened bracket is the first one that has to be closed. Which data structure gives you the most recent item first?
Push every opening bracket. On a closing bracket, check that the top of the stack is its matching opener and pop it. If it is not (or the stack is empty), the string is invalid.
At the end the stack must be empty: `"(("` never has a wrong closing bracket but is still invalid. And a closing bracket must not try to pop from an empty stack.
explanation:
**The idea.** "The most recently opened bracket must be closed first" is last-in, first-out, which is exactly a stack. Push every opening bracket. On a closing bracket, the top of the stack must be its matching opener: pop it, otherwise the string is invalid. At the end the stack must be empty, or some bracket was never closed.

**Edge cases to name.** The empty string (valid), a lone closer such as `"]"` (there is nothing to pop), leftover openers such as `"(("`, and `")("` (the right counts in the wrong order).

**Complexity.** O(n) time and O(n) space. Repeatedly deleting `"()"`, `"[]"` and `"{}"` from the string also gives the right answer, but each deletion pass is O(n) and a deeply nested string needs n/2 passes: O(n²), which the large tests expose.

**Follow-up.** Return the index of the first bracket that breaks the rule (store indexes on the stack), the way an editor underlines the error.
